conventions.convention: R is a commutative ring, q is a unit, n ≥ 0, and all Hecke modules are right modules. The quadratic normalization is (T_i−q)(T_i+1)=0; star fixes T_i and sends T_w to T_(w⁻¹).
The right tableau action is (t·σ)(c)=σ⁻¹(t(c)). The distinguished permutation d(t) satisfies t^λ·d(t)=t; w_λ satisfies t^λ·w_λ=t_λ. D_λ consists of the minimal representatives of cosets S_λ d.
x_λ=Σ_(w∈S_λ)T_w, y_λ=Σ_(w∈S_λ)(−q)^(−ℓ(w))T_w, z_λ=x_λ T_(w_λ)y_(λ′), M(λ)=x_λH, and P(λ)=z_λH. The permutation form has diagonal β(x_λT_d,x_λT_e)=δ_(d,e)q^ℓ(d); the DJ form is its restriction.
θ(T_i)=(q−1)−T_i=−qT_i⁻¹, M^θ has action m·h=mθ(h), and M° has action (f·h)(m)=f(mh*). θ(x_λ)=q^ℓ(w₀(S_λ))y_λ. At q=1, θ is the sign automorphism.

Murphy elements are m_st=T_(d(s))*x_λT_(d(t)). Higher ideals use strictly dominating shapes. The right cell action fixes the first index, and the form is defined by m_us m_tv ≡ G_λ(m_s,m_t)m_uv modulo the higher ideal.

Polytabloid basis vectors are e_t=z_λT_(d_(λ′)(t)), indexed by standard tableaux of the conjugate shape. In the embedding expansion, r≤t′ means every row-prefix count of labels ≤m in r is at most the corresponding count in t′. Unit triangularity concerns the embedding minor and does not assert nonsingularity of the DJ Gram matrix.

The comparison is normalized by Φ_λ(z_λ)=m₀, with G_(λ′)^θ(Φ_λx,Φ_λy)=q^(N−L)β(x,y), where N=ℓ(w₀(S_(λ′))) and L=ℓ(w_λ). D denotes the form quotient; an identically zero form gives a zero form quotient without asserting a zero actual module head.

At q=1 the classical left Specht action is converted to a right action by x·w=w⁻¹x. The Schur dictionary is conditional on an independently proved corner sending W(λ) to C_M(λ) and L(λ) to D_M(λ); its ordinary conjugate dictionary retains θ.

load_bearing.statement: For every commutative ring R and unit q, the standard Murphy elements form an R-basis of H; their dominance spans are two-sided ideals; C_M(λ)=M(λ)/(M(λ)∩I^(strictly dominating λ)) is free on the standard fixed-first-index classes and satisfies the first-index-independent cell law. Its Murphy form is symmetric and contravariant, and all these constructions commute with base change.

For every commutative ring R, unit q, and λ⊢n with μ=λ′, the vectors e_t=z_λT_(d_μ(t)), t∈Std(μ), form an R-basis of P(λ). Their row-module expansion has leading term q^ℓ(d_μ(t))b_(t′) and strictly lower terms, giving a unit triangular minor and a split inclusion P(λ)⊆M(λ). The signed Garnir identities and all clauses survive every base change.

For every commutative ring R, unit q, and partitions α,ν⊢n, if Σ_(i≤k)α_i>Σ_(i≤k)ν′_i for some k≥1, then x_αHy_ν=0. This is a universal Laurent-polynomial identity, including singular parameters, with no cancellation of q+1.

For every commutative ring R, unit q, and λ⊢n, there is a base-change-compatible right-H-module isomorphism Φ_λ:P(λ)→C_M(λ′)^θ with Φ_λ(z_λ)=m₀ and G_(λ′)^θ(Φ_λx,Φ_λy)=q^(N−L)β_(P(λ))(x,y). It identifies form radicals and quotients, including zero quotients, and gives P(λ′)≅P(λ)^(°,θ).

For every commutative ring R, unit q, and λ⊢n, B_λ(m_s,p)=β(x_λT_(d_λ(s)),p) defines a perfect H-balanced pairing C_M(λ)×P(λ)→R, identifying C_M(λ)≅P(λ)°. The row quotient kernel is P(λ)⊥=M(λ)∩I^(strictly dominating λ). No nondegeneracy of the DJ self-form is required.

θ(T_i)=(q−1)−T_i=−qT_i⁻¹ defines an involutive automorphism commuting with star and base change. Pullback by θ is exact and preserves simplicity and composition multiplicities. Star duality commutes with base change for finite free modules and with θ. For every λ, θ(x_λ)=q^ℓ(w₀(S_λ))y_λ.

alerts.finding: The Statement asserts the same-column refinement “T_a m_st ≡ −m_st + Σ_(u ◁ s)c_u m_ut (mod higher shapes)”. Its dominance direction is false. Take q=1 over Q, λ=(2,1), t=t₀=[1 2 / 3], s=[1 3 / 2], and a=1. The labels 1,2 share a column in s, and s is the least-dominant standard tableau of this shape, so the stated sum is empty. Writing x=1+T₁ gives m_(s,t₀)=T₂x and the exact identity T₁m_(s,t₀)+m_(s,t₀)+x=x_(3). Modulo the higher-shape ideal Qx_(3), the action is therefore −m_(s,t₀)−m_(t₀,t₀), with a nonzero correction at the more-dominant tableau t₀. Murphy basis independence shows that this correction does not vanish. The exact group-algebra identity was independently checked. The item's proof step 1.2 also describes corrections as strictly more dominant, contradicting its displayed Statement.

seams_checked.note: The Murphy basis theorem cites the integral basis and fixed-first-index law faithfully. The Specht definition uses S^λ=(S_M^(λ′))^θ, retains the explicit unit-scaled ordinary form comparison, and specializes its factor to 1 at q=1. The Schur theorem preserves the conditional dictionary's conjugation and θ, including zero form quotients. The semistandard-filtration lemma faithfully uses same-shape duality and permutation self-duality to obtain an ordinary Specht filtration; its separate incorrect same-column formula is routed in alerts. The bridge itself imports no Schur theorem or finite-e classifier.

The first-level and induction items use the signed-conjugate form comparison with factor 1 at q=1. The restriction item uses same-shape star duality to transfer a star-fixed central scalar, without identifying ordinary and Murphy form radicals. The general-Hecke and Schur comparison items use the exact symmetric trace and retain restricted Murphy labels and the ordinary conjugate-sign dictionary. The page reaches the bridge through its type-A Hecke prerequisite; its relevant items also cite bridge suppliers directly. No branching theorem is imported into the bridge proofs.

The regime and graded Specht definition distinguish the left Murphy module, obtained through star, from ordinary P(μ). They state separately S(μ)≅P(μ)° and S(μ)≅P(μ′)^θ as ungraded comparisons. The head theorem retains the signed conjugate ordinary label and unit-preserved radicals. The regime proves residue reflection locally using the multiplicative JM palindrome; it does not assume that raw θ is homogeneous in the transported grading. Characteristic and grading qualifications are preserved, and the bridge supplies no graded or crystal-label theorem.
